findings.summary: Incomplete-tail recovery still loses acknowledged records when the interrupted append leaves a complete JSON object without its terminating newline. load() accepts that object and performs no repair because JSON decoding succeeds. The next append concatenates another object onto it; subsequent reconstruction rejects the combined line, losing the newly acknowledged request and the preceding record. Normalize a non-newline-terminated valid tail before accepting further writes, preserving its record, and add an isolated load/append/reload regression. This violates durable acceptance and interruption recovery under behaviors 1 and 7 and P6.

The cross-call done guard still forgets required deliveries that returned NOT_READY. _deliver marks NOT_READY final, and outstanding_deliveries retires every final result regardless of whether delivery occurred. Consequently, with queued requests A and B, A's requested reply can return NOT_READY from the default unbound reply port, then B's empty done list produces a done verdict although no reply was delivered and Goal never explicitly retired that obligation. The new UNKNOWN regression does not cover this path. Separate finality of an attempt from fulfillment or explicit disposition of its required delivery, and add the two-request NOT_READY regression, including reconstruction. This violates P4 without requiring any live service testing.

Continuous review rc-fd534f3a-a786-5dd4-b981-4bf31e4e9f48 independently records APPROVE for implementation subject d0225b647c9f0da1b5dfde49a6fdb80b58426e24, with an unwired version-activation note. Final independently records REJECT for the development-stage defects above. Static inspection confirms that the latest implementation added the reversed-order repository-admission guard and cross-call UNKNOWN-delivery tracking.

The supplied input_commit and subject_commit are identical full RC identities, and the distinct implementation_subject_commit matches the current Continuous artifact. No shell or Git command was executed. Product-tree equality between I and RC could not be mechanically verified with the available file-inspection tools; actual HEAD verification remains with the deterministic seal. The committed implement handoff names actor work_head_commit d2e6da4a33b4a7797227e25aeabf6f2c0fa548ec, unlike the supplied product-commit label, so that metadata-only ancestry/product consistency also remains unverified rather than inferred from SHA equality.

The feedback index and all ten review artifacts present in the reviews directory were inspected, but several single-line JSON records were truncated by the inspection tools. The requested immutable feedback/history.json archive is absent. Complete historical feedback verification therefore cannot be claimed.

The committed handoff reports compileall exit 0, 51 passing kernel tests, and 10 passing wiring tests; these are implementer-reported results, not checks executed by Final. Its verification record does not include the required cwd, timestamps, stdout, or stderr. Real Runtime binding, reply delivery, process recovery/cancellation, Session queries, integration, deployment, and joint E2E remain unrun and deferred under the experiment constraints. This verdict does not demand those forbidden checks or claim production acceptance or whole-Goal ready_for_joint_validation.
